I opened the issue in pit: [cv/pit#368](https://github.com/cv/pit/issues/368), titled "A JSON-encoded string in params reaches a string input still encoded". I checked that its description shows as plain Markdown, not wrapped in quotes.

It contains:
- **What happened:** the PR body for #76 reached the program still JSON-encoded, so `gh pr create --body` posted it with the quotes and `\n` escapes. It links the run that did it ([43522489097](https://github.com/cv/pi-action/actions/runs/43522489097)).
- **Proposed fix:** a patch for `resolveToolInput` with two new tests. The patch applies to pit's `main`, where `test/tool/input.test.ts` passes (19 tests). It notes the downside: a program that really wants literal quotes around its input would get them removed.

Creating the issue worked even though GitHub reports no permissions for this token on `cv/pit`. Pushing a branch or forking still fails, so I still can't open a PR there.
